replies.author: HeyYou_GetOffMyCloud
replies.body:
In mine Ive been building with opus and asking it to delegate to sonnet and haiku where possible, and then at stages where I want to review I'll ask it to spin up several fabel agents to read only review areas like code, level design, art direction, UI etc.

Then I get opus to create a questionnaire for me to give answers to on the comments. Works pretty nicely for fast progress

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body:
>In mine Ive been building with opus and asking it to delegate to sonnet and haiku where possible.

There's no need to do this, you're just burning tokens by forcing a context reset. Be very cautious and conservative about doing this sort of thing.

comments.author: ThinkTyler
comments.body: Everyone always says Opus 5.5 but I’ve been using Sonnet 5.5 Ultracode and I find it works just as well as Opus. I setup pretty detailed instructions and guardrails. I give it tasks to do while I sleep, then I do play tests when I’m awake in my spare time and give it feedback. Seems to be doing really well and uses a lot less usage than Opus.  I think it’s more about how good you are with setting up structure and providing feedback when it comes to these frontier models, but this is anecdotal I haven’t A/B tested it or anything.

replies.author: ThinkTyler
replies.body:
Not my experience, but who is “they” though?

I use Claude platform for work and it’s dollar based and we each get a monthly spend between $2000-$5000 depending on our role.  Whenever I use opus to vibe code overnight it spends like $500-800 and sonnet is only like $100.

Then for my personal stuff I have the max plan but only the $100 one and I can run it every night without any usage issues. I used Opus one night for a similar thing and my weekly usage was gone in one night.

So that’s my anecdotal evidence.

I think it’s more about the guardrails and structure though because Opus does a ton of review layers by default. It’s also geared toward being a deep research model and Sonnet is supposed to be the every day workhorse model.

replies.author: Ok_Perception2387
replies.body: Have you tried using opus 5.5 xhigh, you will love it

replies.author: ThinkTyler
replies.body: Yes, I’ve done tons of long runs with it. With ultracode too. I just don’t see a big difference between opus and sonnet, I can get sonnet to perform just as good with the right instructions and guardrails and it doesn’t wreck my usage as much

replies.author: Ok_Perception2387
replies.body: Ok, you need to understand the use of models and its effort applications. Suppose you are building a game, the first prompt always is harder to generate into output. So, opus 5.5 is the good option, next thing like adding an item, character etc will be acted by the sonnet. In the second prompt, whether you use opus or sonnet, it doesn't differ much. Choose your own way

replies.author: ThinkTyler
replies.body: Yup that is my understanding, I work in AI for my main job, so I use these models constantly.  I’ve even used fable for a game dev first prompt and sonnet for all following ones. I was challenging everyone saying Opus 5.5 in this thread as the default always. There’s nuance and it depends on your ability to setup structure and guardrails. If you are one promoting or initial promoting though then Opus will get it done, at least to a proof of concept level.
